title: G2: Two-state reduction to scalars $(a_y,b_y)$ and the achievable region

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Claim to prove.** For a rank-one POVM $E_y=w_y|\phi_y\rangle\langle\phi_y|$, the joint statistics — hence $I(X;Y)$ — depend on $E_y$ only through
$$a_y=\operatorname{tr}(\sigma E_y),\quad b_y=\operatorname{tr}(\Delta E_y),\quad \sigma=p_1\rho_1+p_2\rho_2,\ \Delta=p_1\rho_1-p_2\rho_2.$$
Then $\Pr(X{=}1,Y{=}y)=\tfrac{a_y+b_y}{2}$, $\Pr(X{=}2,Y{=}y)=\tfrac{a_y-b_y}{2}$, so $\sum_y a_y=1$, $\sum_y b_y=p_1-p_2$.

**What must be characterized.** The exact achievable set of $\{(a_y,b_y)\}$ over rank-one POVMs. The constraints are NOT only the two linear sums: positivity needs $|b_y|\le a_y$, and the operator constraint $\sum_y w_y|\phi_y\rangle\langle\phi_y|=I$ couples directions. State the region and its extreme points.

**Pitfall.** Forgetting the operator constraint $\sum_y E_y=I$ (strictly stronger than the two scalar sums) — this is exactly what forces orthogonality in G3 and separates $N=2$ from $N\ge3$.
